gap: No result ChatGPT got states that LB Tech Reviews measured the JBL Spinner BT, one of ChatGPT's three picks, at 33.15 rpm (-0.55%) with 0.75% wow and flutter, enough that 'you can hear a piano note fluctuate in pitch'.
standout_why: turntableverse.com (opened 2026-11-13) gives only maker wow-and-flutter specs (AT-LP70XBT <0.25%, AT-LP120XBT-USB <0.2%, Pro-Ject E1 BT 0.25%/0.23%) and one reviewer figure, What Hi-Fi's 'at least 15 metres' Bluetooth range for the Sony PS-LX310BT. It has no measured speed, wow and flutter, rumble or latency for any model, and it does not cover the JBL Spinner BT. I could not read the body of either cited page: WebFetch returned only the title for whathifi.com's Bluetooth turntable guide and for loudersound.com's record-player guide. vinylpickup.com failed with a certificate error. So I have not confirmed what those three pages say. From search snippets, vinylpickup may print a speed reading for the non-Bluetooth AT-LP70X, but not for the Spinner BT.
decides: This measurement counts against the JBL Spinner BT, which ChatGPT's second answer called 'Best for style and manual control' at $349.95. A 0.75% wow and flutter reading is about three times Audio-Technica's <0.25% ceiling for the AT-LP70XBT (that is a spec, not a measurement), and the reviewer heard the pitch waver. It supports ChatGPT's choice of the AT-LP70XBT as the default pick, but only by comparing the JBL measurement with a maker spec. I found no independent measured wow and flutter for the AT-LP70XBT, AT-LP60XBT or Sony PS-LX3BT, so this is not a full side-by-side. One caveat: LB Tech tested a single unit in 2023 and did not name its instrument or the weighting used.
